adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:288 — The `.reply .username a` light-theme branch changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 70%, unintentionally dimming the light theme; only the dark-theme source should change.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at line 288-291 in desktop/topic-post.scss, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme branch (first argument to dark-light-choose) changed from 30% lightness to 70% lightness, which would significantly dim the text in light theme. This appears to be an error - the pattern used elsewhere in the diff maintains the original lightness value for the light theme and only adds the dark theme alternative. For example, other similar changes keep the original value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This specific line incorrectly flipped the lightness value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:179 — The `a.star h3` light-theme branch changes from 20% to 50% lightness; it should retain 20% while only the dark-theme branch is substituted.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme branch changed from 20% to 50% lightness. This appears to be an inconsistency - the original value was 20% lightness, but the new dark-light-choose uses 50% for the light theme. This is likely a mistake where the developer should have kept 20% for the light theme: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` reverses both values (`$primary` 70% becomes 30% and `$secondary` 30% becomes 70%), unlike the desktop rule and causing incorrect contrast in both themes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies an inconsistency. In mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This reverses the lightness values compared to the desktop version in desktop/modal.scss line 50, which changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The mobile version uses 30%/70% while desktop uses 70%/30%, which is inconsistent and likely a mistake that would cause incorrect contrast.
